newsitem.title: ITALY: PRESS DIGEST - Italy - Monday June 2.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Italy - Monday June 2.

text.p: The following are some of the top headlines in leading Italian newspapers.

* Italy's centre-left government welcomed the French election result won by the socialist-led opposition. Prime Minister Romano Prodi said European political scene was finally changing for a new direction (all).

* The Italian government revoked the nomination of a new ambassador to Albania, casting confusion on its leading role in European efforts to check its turbulent eastern neighbour's slide into anarchy (all).

* Treasury minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi said the Italian economy was heading in the right direction, as the centre-left government's three-year economic programme (DPEF) was supported by Bank of Italy's governor Antonio Fazio (Corriere della Sera).

* In an interview, Giorgio Fossa, chairman of employers body Confindustria, said the European single currency should not be delayed under any circumstances and urged prime minister Prodi to speed up welfare state reforms, saying the DPEF did not contain guidelines for reforms of the public sector spending (La Repubblica).
Reuters has not verified these stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
